thought_title: The Bond of Love in Christ
orientation: The Roman church is exhorting the Corinthians to pursue love, which it presents as the bond that unites believers to God and perfects the elect.
pass_a_gloss: The [one] having love in Christ let him do the commandments of Christ. The bond of the love of God who is able to explain? The greatness of the beauty of it who [is] sufficient to tell out? The height, into which love leads up, [is] beyond telling. Love glues us to God, love covers a multitude of sins, love endures all things, is patient with all things: nothing vulgar [is] in love, nothing proud: love does not have division, love does not make faction, love does all things in harmony: in love were perfected all the elect of God, without love nothing [is] well-pleasing to God. In love the Master received us: because of the love, which he had toward us, his blood he gave on behalf of us, Jesus Christ our Lord, in the will of God, and the flesh on behalf of our flesh and the soul on behalf of our souls.

choices.why: The verb is concrete and physical; 'glues' preserves the vividness of the Greek rather than a more abstract 'unites' or 'joins.'
The compound means literally 'not-out-narratable'; 'beyond telling' keeps the sense of something that cannot be fully recounted.
The Greek term refers to what is base or mechanical, illiberal; 'vulgar' captures the moral and social lowliness without modern class overtones.
The glossary mandates 'division' for σχίσμα, distinguishing it from στάσις ('faction').
The glossary mandates 'faction' for στάσις; the verb στασιάζω is rendered as 'make faction' to keep the noun connection visible.
The passive aorist indicates a completed action done to the elect; 'were perfected' preserves the passive and the perfective sense.

pass_b_english: Let the one who has love in Christ do what Christ commands.
Who can explain the bond of God's love?
Who is able to tell the greatness of its beauty?
The height to which love leads is beyond telling.

Love glues us to God. Love covers a multitude of sins (1 Peter 4:8). Love endures all things, is patient with all things (1 Corinthians 13:7). There is nothing vulgar in love, nothing arrogant. Love has no division. Love does not make faction. Love does everything in harmony. In love all the elect of God were perfected. Without love nothing is pleasing to God.
In love the Master received us. Because of the love he had for us, Jesus Christ our Lord gave his blood for us by the will of God, and his flesh for our flesh, and his soul for our souls.

last_rejected.quote: In love the Master received us
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐν ἀγάπῃ προσελάβετο ἡμᾶς ὁ δεσπότης
last_rejected.why: προσελάβετο means 'took to himself, received, welcomed'—but in this theological context it refers to Christ's incarnation or adoption of humanity. 'Received' is weak; 'took us to himself' or 'embraced us' would capture the incarnational force better. However 'received' is within semantic range. Not a clear error.
last_rejected.ruling: προσελάβετο = 'received, welcomed'; 'received' is within normal range. Claim itself concedes no clear error.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'ἐκλεκτοί' as 'the elect'. The English has 'the elect of God' which matches glossary exactly. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: οἱ ἐκλεκτοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ = 'the elect of God'; matches glossary exactly. No error.

last_rejected.quote: Love endures all things, is patient with all things (1 Corinthians 13:7).
last_rejected.why: 1 Cor 13:7 is bears/believes/hopes/endures. Patience (μακροθυμεῖ) is 13:4, not 13:7, and not “with all things.”
last_rejected.fix: Love bears with all things and is patient with all things (1 Corinthians 13:4, 7).
last_rejected.ruling: Source ἀγάπη πάντα ἀνέχεται, πάντα μακροθυμεῖ is 1 Clement's own wording. 'Patient with all things' renders πάντα μακροθυμεῖ literally. The 13:7 cite matches πάντα ὑπομένει/ἀνέχεται loosely; minor.
